tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Zero-dimensional homology of path-connected space] ↗ prop:homology-disjoint-union 1. ch2:2.7\group Singular Homology

If $X$ is nonempty and path-connected, $H_0(X)\cong \mathbb {Z}$. In general, $H_0(X)$ is a direct sum of one copy of $\mathbb {Z}$ for each path-component.
Proof

\sketch The augmentation $\varepsilon :C_0(X)\to \mathbb {Z}$ sums coefficients. Path-connectedness supplies a path from a chosen basepoint to every point, showing $\ker \varepsilon =\operatorname {Im}\partial _1$.

□
